arxiv-2101-08705.title: Assessing the Benefits of Model Ensembles in Neural Re-Ranking for Passage Retrieval Thanks: This research was supported by Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia (FCT), through the Ph.D. scholarship with reference SFRH/BD/150497/2019, and the INESC-ID multi-annual funding from the PIDDAC programme (U
arxiv-2101-08705.creator: Luís Borges, Bruno Martins, Jamie Callan
arxiv-2101-08705.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Luís Borges, Bruno Martins, Jamie Callan. Our work aimed at experimentally assessing the benefits of model ensembling within the context of neural methods for passage re-ranking. Starting from relatively standard neural models, we use a previous technique named Fast Geometric Ensembling to generate multiple model instances from particular training schedules, then focusing or attention on different types of approaches for combining the results from the multiple model instances (e.g., averaging the ranking scores, using fusion methods from the IR literature, or using supervised learning-to-rank).

arxiv-2201-09204.title: α \alpha -Fairness User Pairing for Downlink NOMA Systems with Imperfect Successive Interference Cancellation
arxiv-2201-09204.creator: Nemalidinne Siva Mouni, Pavan Reddy M., Abhinav Kumar, and Prabhat K. Upadhyay
arxiv-2201-09204.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nemalidinne Siva Mouni, Pavan Reddy M., Abhinav Kumar, and Prabhat K. Upadhyay. Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is considered as one of the predominant multiple access technique for the next-generation cellular networks. We consider a 2-user pair downlink NOMA system with imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). We consider bounds on the power allocation factors and then formulate the power allocation as an optimization problem to achieve α \alpha -Fairness among the paired users.

arxiv-2309-15136.title: A multi-modal approach for identifying schizophrenia using cross-modal attention Thanks: This work was supported by the National Science Foundation grant numbered 2124270.
arxiv-2309-15136.creator: Gowtham Premananth, Yashish M.Siriwardena, Philip Resnik, Carol Espy-Wilson
arxiv-2309-15136.description: Abstract This study focuses on how different modalities of human communication can be used to distinguish between healthy controls and subjects with schizophrenia who exhibit strong positive symptoms. We developed a multi-modal schizophrenia classification system using audio, video, and text.

arxiv-2311-06016.title: Spontaneous Vibrations and Stochastic Resonance of Short Oligomeric Springs
arxiv-2311-06016.creator: Alexey M. Astakhov, Vladislav S. Petrovskii ID, Maria A. Frolkina ID, Anastasia A. Markina ID, Alexander D. Muratov ID, Alexander F. Valov, Vladik A. Avetisov ID
arxiv-2311-06016.description: Abstract There is growing interest in molecular structures that exhibit dynamics similar to bistable mechanical systems. These structures have the potential to be used as two-state operating units for various functional purposes. Particularly intriguing are the bistable systems that display spontaneous vibrations and stochastic resonance.

arxiv-2412-03433.title: Genetic Algorithm Based System for Path Planning with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Swarms in Cell-Grid Environments
arxiv-2412-03433.creator: Alejandro Puente-Castro, Enrique Fernandez-Blanco, Daniel Rivero
arxiv-2412-03433.description: Abstract Path Planning methods for autonomously controlling swarms of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are gaining momentum due to their operational advantages. An increasing number of scenarios now require autonomous control of multiple UAVs, as autonomous operation can significantly reduce labor costs. Additionally, obtaining optimal flight paths can lower energy consumption, thereby extending battery life for other critical operations.

arxiv-2506-00944.title: Photon-induced production of the exotic charged charmonium-like state Z c ​ ( 3900 ) Z_{c}(3900) off nuclear targets and its internal structure
arxiv-2506-00944.creator: E. Ya. Paryev
arxiv-2506-00944.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the possibility to study the famous charged charmonium-like state Z c ​ ( 3900 ) Z_{c}(3900) production off nuclear targets and its properties in inclusive photon-induced reactions near the kinematic threshold within the collision model based on the nuclear spectral function.

arxiv-2508-02867.creator: Hannes Jakob
arxiv-2508-02867.description: Abstract . Relative to class many supercompact cardinals, we construct a model of 𝖹𝖥𝖢 + 𝖦𝖢𝖧 \mathsf{ZFC}+\mathsf{GCH} where for every singular cardinal δ \delta of countable cofinality and every regular uncountable μ < δ \mu<\delta there are stationarily many non-approachable points of cofinality μ \mu in δ + \delta^{+} .

pmc-10487872.title: Pharmacological Inhibition and Genetic Deletion of Cystathionine Gamma-Lyase in Mice Protects against Organ Injury in Sepsis: A Key Role of Adhesion Molecules on Endothelial Cells
pmc-10487872.creator: Sumeet Manandhar, Stephen Chambers, Andrew Miller, Isao Ishii, Madhav Bhatia, Maurizio Battino
pmc-10487872.description: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), synthesized by cystathionine gamma-lyase (Cth), contributes to the inflammatory response observed in sepsis. This study examines the effect of Cth-derived H2S in adhesion molecules on endothelial cells of vital organs in mice in a cecal ligation puncture (CLP)-induced model of sepsis, using two different and complementary approaches: Cth gene deletion and pharmacological inhibition.

pmc-10757164.title: Whole Body Vibration Therapy for Children with Disabilities: A Survey of Potential Risks and Benefits
pmc-10757164.creator: David Godley, John Csongradi
pmc-10757164.description: Highlights•Reviews of Whole Body Vibration literature.•Discusses biological effects of Whole Body Vibration – beneficial and deleterious.•Warns of risks of Whole Body Vibration for children.•Makes suggestions for future Whole Body Vibration research.KEYWORDS: Rehabilitation, Whole body vibration, Cerebral palsy, Spasticity, Exercise, Mobility Background It is well established that mechanical vibration can have beneficial as well as harmful effects in humans.

pmc-11344860.title: Effect of nutrition education on the nutritional status of pregnant women in Robe and Goba Towns, Southeast Ethiopia, using a cluster randomized controlled trial
pmc-11344860.creator: Girma Beressa, Susan J. Whiting, Tefera Belachew
pmc-11344860.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Maternal malnutrition is pervasive throughout the world, notably in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), including Ethiopia. This study aimed to assess the effect of nutrition education on the nutritional status of pregnant women in urban settings in Southeast Ethiopia. A community-based two-arm parallel cluster randomized controlled trial was conducted among 447 randomly selected pregnant women attending antenatal care (224 intervention and 223 control). We used a multistage cluster sampling technique followed by systematic sampling to select the pregnant women.

pmc-11529683.title: Two-child limit in the UK: where policy meets poverty
pmc-11529683.creator: Jatinder Hayre
pmc-11529683.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). or subsequent child born after April 2017, no additional welfare assistance is provided; plunging many large, low-income families deeper into financial deprivation: the most vulnerable in society shouldering the greatest burden of austerity. While the policy may offer an immediate cost-saving exercise to the Government, of up to £3455 a year per child per family,1 it disregards the profound long-term, deleterious impacts on child health, development and economic sustainability.

pmc-11655340.title: Clonally unrelated HL-type RS manifested as hemophagocytic syndrome: a case report and literature review
pmc-11655340.creator: Xiaoman Zheng, Wenshuang Ding, Zhigang Zhu, Junping Li, Weijie Zhong
pmc-11655340.description: Hodgkin lymphoma variant of Richter syndrome (HL-type RS) is a very rare disease, in which chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) is transformed into novel Hodgkin lymphoma. The most important prognostic factor of HL-type RS is the clonal relationship between HL-type RS and the preexisting CLL/SLL.

pmc-12445227.title: Targeting long non-coding RNA MALAT1 preserves endothelial cell integrity and protects against kidney fibrosis
pmc-12445227.creator: Qiao Zhao, Loïs A.K. van der Pluijm, Morgane Gourvest, Atefeh Lafzi, Daniel Peled, Whitney G. Rubin, Juliette A. de Klerk, Roderick C. Slieker, Leen M. ’t Hart, Wendy Stam, Annemarie M. van Oeveren-Rietdijk, Jacques M.G.J. Duijs, Angela Koudijs, Joris I. Rotmans, Hilal Kazan, Anton Jan van Zonneveld
pmc-12445227.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Loss of integrity of the capillary network is directly associated with the development of kidney fibrosis resulting in chronic kidney disease. Here, we characterized long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in endothelial cells (ECs) during the development of kidney fibrosis. Using a murine EC lineage-tracing model, we observed expression of the conserved lncRNA metastasis-associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript 1 (Malat1) to be elevated in ECs upon kidney injury; either by ischemia-reperfusion injury or by unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO).

pmc-12572778.title: Papillary fibroelastoma of the papillary muscle—a case report on a rare entity and sometimes a delayed diagnosis
pmc-12572778.creator: Jules Miazza, Oliver Reuthebuch, Thierry Carrel, Cristiano Spadaccio, Mihai Strachinaru, Edgar Ramírez-Vázquez, Jean-Luc Maigrot, Giorgia Benzoni
pmc-12572778.description: BackgroundPapillary fibroelastoma, generally affecting the valve endocardium, is one of the most common benign cardiac tumours. Although rarely reported, atypical localization of such tumours complexifies diagnosis and might negatively impact patient outcomes due to late detection.Case summaryWe present the case of a 69-year-old female patient presenting for a check-up consultation and reporting symptoms of dysesthesia, aphasia, and dizziness.

pmc-13100903.title: Genetic drift acts strongly on influenza virus populations within acute human infections but is obscured by other factors within acutely infected swine
pmc-13100903.creator: Yike T Shi, Michael A Martin, Daniel B Weissman, Katia Koelle
pmc-13100903.description: The evolutionary dynamics of seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs) have been well characterized at the population level, with antigenic drift known to be a major force in driving strain turnover. The evolution of IAV populations at the within-host level, however, is still less well characterized.

pmc-13109294.title: panomiX: Investigating mechanisms of trait emergence through multi-omics data integration
pmc-13109294.creator: Ankur Sahu, Dennis Psaroudakis, Hardy Rolletschek, Kerstin Neumann, Ljudmilla Borisjuk, Axel Himmelbach, Kalyan Pinninti, Dominic Knoch, Nadine Töpfer, Jędrzej Szymański
pmc-13109294.description: Complex omics approaches and high-throughput phenotyping generate large, heterogeneous datasets that make linking molecular signatures to plant traits challenging. To address this challenge, here we introduce panomiX, a user-friendly toolbox for multi-omics integration, designed to enable non-experts to apply advanced computational methods with ease.

pmc-13266397.title: Locally advanced breast cancer in an elderly male with end-stage renal disease: A case report
pmc-13266397.creator: Mengfan Chen, Ming Feng, Xiaoyu Li, Huanhuan Wang, Ke Hong, Chang Yao
pmc-13266397.description: Male breast cancer (MBC) is uncommon, often diagnosed late and prone to distant metastases. Treating MBC is more challenging than treating female breast cancer. The present study reports a case of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in a Chinese patient with locally advanced MBC.

pmc-13542989.title: Urban Stone Marten (Martes foina)–Human Conflicts: A Longitudinal Survey‐Based Approach to a Persistent Challenge
pmc-13542989.creator: Michał Strączyński, Sayantani M. Basak, Paweł Kwapisz, Joanna Tusznio, Jesse S. Lewis, Izabela A. Wierzbowska
pmc-13542989.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Although stone martens ( Martes foina ) are widely recognised for causing urban property damage, including damage done when entering and tearing up car engine compartments, the human dimensions of these conflicts remain largely understudied. Based on interviews with local car mechanics in Krakow, Poland conducted in 2010 and 2023, we explored the long‐term human‐stone marten interaction through the lens of the car damage conflict.

pmc-13711406.title: Study on the anti-asthmatic effect of Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair and its mechanisms in regulating the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway
pmc-13711406.creator: Qianru Yang, Xiaoxue Chen, Jintong Cai, Zhengwen Xie, Yuhan Nie, Jinghui Sun, He Li, Chunmei Wang
pmc-13711406.description: BackgroundGinseng-Schisandra herb pair is a classic representative one of the “combination of tonification and astringency” in traditional Chinese medicine. Ginseng tonifies lung Qi and benefits heart Qi, while Schisandra restrains the lung, nourishes the kidney, calms the mind, and soothes the spirit.
